quizName: DMV Practice Test #16 30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: What should you do when riding at night?

options.text: Ride on the shoulder of the road.

questions.explanation: At night, increase your following distance. Slow down and be ready to change your lane position.

questions.question: What should be part of your normal scanning routine while riding?

options.text: Constantly looking in the rearview mirror.

questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often as part of your normal routine. Also check mirrors before changing lanes, at intersections, and before slowing down.

questions.question: What should you do when the lights on a railroad crossing sign are flashing?

options.text: Stop and wait until the train passes.
Turn around and find an alternate route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait until the train passes.
questions.explanation: Stop completely at a railroad crossing with flashing lights. Wait until the train passes and the lights stop flashing before you go. Never try to beat a train across the tracks.

questions.question: How should a motorcycle be parked on the road?

options.text: Create an angle with the curb that is between 45 and 90 degrees.
Be parked without a wheel or fender touching the curb.
Be parked parallel to the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Create an angle with the curb that is between 45 and 90 degrees.
questions.explanation: Park your motorcycle at an angle between 45 and 90 degrees to the curb. A wheel or fender should touch the curb.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell you about upcoming road conditions. This sign warns that a stop sign is coming.

questions.question: What is the minimum following distance when riding at night?
questions.explanation: At night, it is hard to judge distance in the dark. Keep at least three seconds of distance between you and the vehicle ahead.

questions.question: What should you do when being passed on the left?

options.text: Ride in the right portion of the lane.
Ride in the center portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed. Riding on the right side can be dangerous because it may cause the passing driver to return to your lane too quickly.

questions.question: What should you NOT do when reacting to a hazard in the road?

options.text: Make your presence known by sounding your horn and/or using lights or signals.

questions.explanation: Tell other drivers about hazards by using your horn, lights, and signals. Change your speed to match the situation. Move your lane position or change direction if needed.

questions.question: Where is there the greatest risk of conflict between a motorcycle and other traffic?
questions.explanation: Intersections are where motorcycles are most likely to have conflicts with other vehicles. Be very careful when entering an intersection.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are white with red and black markings. They show traffic laws for that area. This sign means U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: How can you reduce your reaction time?

options.text: Ride slower than the speed limit.
Shift into neutral when slowing down.
Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
questions.explanation: When approaching an intersection, ride carefully. Keep your hands ready on the clutch and both brakes so you can stop quickly if needed.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing your motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Slow down and let the dog get close, then speed up and ride away.
Stop and wait for the dog to leave.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let the dog get close, then speed up and ride away.
questions.explanation: Dogs are attracted to motorcycles. If a dog chases you, slow down and shift to a lower gear. As the dog gets close, accelerate and leave it behind.

questions.question: What is the best formation for a group of motorcyclists to stay together safely?
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is the best way for a group to ride together. It keeps riders close while giving each rider enough safe space.

questions.question: Before you start riding, make sure the fuel valve is:
questions.explanation: Always open the fuel valve before starting your ride. If it is closed, the engine may start using fuel left in the lines, but it will stall when that fuel runs out.

questions.question: A motorized scooter can:

options.text: Only be used during the day.
Be used without a driver license.
Be used with any type of driver license.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be used with any type of driver license.
questions.explanation: In California, a motorized scooter can be used by anyone who has any class of driver license.

questions.question: When other vehicles are slowed or stopped, what should a motorcyclist do?

options.text: Not weave between lanes of traffic.
Weave in and out of traffic lanes.
Ride in a straight line between two lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not weave between lanes of traffic.
questions.explanation: Riding between rows of stopped or slow-moving vehicles is dangerous. Cars may change lanes, doors may open, or arms may stick out. Motorcycles need the full width of a lane to be safe.

questions.question: In which lane position are motorcyclists usually easiest to see?
questions.explanation: The center lane position is usually best when following a car. It places you in the driver's rearview mirror where they can see you. Be ready to change position if traffic or conditions change.

questions.question: Small vehicles appear to be ________ and slower than they really are.
questions.explanation: It is hard to judge the speed and distance of small vehicles like motorcycles. Do not assume that drivers of larger vehicles can accurately see your speed and location.

questions.question: A person with a blood alcohol content (BAC) of ____ is considered intoxicated.
questions.explanation: In Virginia, a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher means you are intoxicated. You cannot legally drive any motor vehicle if you are intoxicated.

questions.question: Which brake is stronger on a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: The front brake is stronger than the rear brake. It provides at least 70 percent of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: When carrying a load on your motorcycle, where should it be placed?

options.text: On the gas tank in front of you.
Against the sissy bar or frame on the back of the seat.

questions.explanation: Place loads over or in front of the rear axle. Only experienced riders should carry loads on a motorcycle.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers that right turns are not allowed. Red and black signs with white backgrounds show traffic laws.

questions.question: What is the maximum engine displacement for a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: A motorcycle is any two- or three-wheeled vehicle with an engine of 125 cubic centimeters or less. You need a motorcycle license to operate one.

questions.question: When passing a truck on a two-lane road, when should you return to your lane?

options.text: When you can see the entire front of the truck in your rearview mirror.
As soon as the truck is behind you.
When you feel you have enough space.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see the entire front of the truck in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Only return to your lane when you can see the entire front of the truck in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: How should a group of motorcyclists pass another vehicle?
questions.explanation: On a two-lane road, each motorcyclist should pass one at a time. Wait until one rider finishes passing before the next one begins.

questions.question: Why is it dangerous to ride directly next to another vehicle?

options.text: The other vehicle may block your escape route.
Other drivers can easily see you.
You may not be able to read road signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: The other vehicle may block your escape route.
questions.explanation: Riding alongside another vehicle is dangerous. The vehicle could move into your lane or block your escape route if a hazard appears.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing you, what should you do?

options.text: Stop your motorcycle and wait for the animal to lose interest.
Slow down as the dog approaches, then quickly speed up and drive away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down as the dog approaches, then quickly speed up and drive away.
questions.explanation: When a dog approaches, slow down and downshift. Then quickly speed up and drive away as the dog gets close.

questions.question: What should you do when riding at night?

options.text: Stay close to the vehicle in front of you to use its lights.
Keep your normal speed to avoid being hit from behind.
Slow down and stay farther behind other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stay farther behind other vehicles.
questions.explanation: At night, reduce speed and increase your distance from other vehicles. It is harder to see, and you need more time and space to react to hazards.

questions.question: A motorcycle's brake light is _________ a car's brake light.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle's brake light is usually harder to see than a car's brake light, especially when the taillight is on. Other drivers may not notice when you brake.

questions.question: What usually causes a "wobble" (shaking of the front wheel and handlebars)?

options.text: Incorrect tire pressure or uneven loading.
The front wheel not being tightened correctly to the frame.
Hitting an object with the front tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Incorrect tire pressure or uneven loading.
questions.explanation: A wobble is when the front wheel and handlebars shake side to side. It is usually caused by improper loading, wrong accessories, or incorrect tire pressure.
